# Ship Two Branches, Not All Eight

**Decision.** Publish **two** of the ten experiment branches as running code, and cover the rest with
written per-branch reports.

**Date.** 2026-07-10, the day the whole tree was imported to git.

## The choice and its criterion

> "Two variants of the agent are included, as requested: **`stable`** (the best result) and
> **`a.bhuiyan`** (the most different architecture). The per-branch reports document the *entire*
> team's work, so nothing is lost by shipping only two code trees."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/README.md, 2026-07-10

The selection rule is stated, and it is not "the two best". It is **best plus most different** —
maximum result and maximum coverage of the design space, which is a deliberately different criterion
from ranking. `stable` is the danger-reward agent with split actor/critic trunks; `a.bhuiyan` is the
offline racing line plus [[residual-reinforcement-learning]] rewrite. Two branches that agree with
each other would have taught a reader nothing.

## The rejected alternatives

- **Ship all ten.** Rejected implicitly by "as requested" — the constraint came from outside. The
  cost would have been real: each tree carries its own ~1500-line environment wrapper, a duplicated
  605-line `snakeoil3_gym.py` and ~0.9 MB of checkpoints.
- **Ship the best only.** Rejected in favour of including the architectural outlier. This is the
  interesting half of the decision, because `a.bhuiyan` is *not* the better performer — its own
  README records that it never completed a clean lap.
- **Ship code and skip the write-ups.** Rejected: the compensation clause — "the per-branch reports
  document the *entire* team's work" — is what makes shipping two trees defensible rather than
  lossy. Eleven markdown files, 846 lines, with tip SHAs, constants tables and reward pseudocode.
  See [[generated-audit-artifact]] and [[branch-per-experiment]].

## The same instinct one paragraph earlier

The README applies the identical logic to the results it reports:

> "Reporting only the best lap would overstate reliability, so consistency was measured over a batch"
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/README.md, 2026-07-10

Best-plus-spread for the numbers, best-plus-most-different for the code. Both are refusals to let a
single flattering artefact stand in for the work — the habit catalogued as
[[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]].

## What the decision actually cost

Six of the branches now exist **only as prose**. Nothing in them is reproducible from this
repository: the `parallel` branch's throughput result has no code behind it, and the report itself
claims only ~9× environment *concurrency* rather than the ~9× rollout throughput the top-level README
reports. The reports are an audit of a *different* repository —
`Szymon1905/AI_racer_pytorch` — and **the tool that produced them was not committed**, so the audit
cannot be re-run either.

There is a softening, too. `project/README.md` describes the `a.bhuiyan` branch as having "reduced
but didn't eliminate" its S-curve errors, where that branch's own README says flatly that it "did not
fully solve the S-curve" and the car "did not finish a clean full lap in the earlier runs". The
top-level page is the more generous of the two. See [[documentation-drift]].
